![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129488/assets/b3c874f3c4564795a2ddcfb4c2896c1bc0ef1b4b7b3d8e8318f42d15643942d7.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $UVWU,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={C}_{1}\cup \{-{C}_{2}\}\cup \{-{C}_{3}\},
$$

where $-{C}_{2}$ and $-{C}_{3}$ are the same paths as ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129488/assets/4d4c2c86ed8506ff034141ac20a5a56587a80370384ceeaf08c66f2ce3e8a315.png)

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a section of the parabola $y=-\sqrt{x}$ from the point $O(0,0)$ to the point $A(4,-2),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a line segment from the point $A(4,-2)$ to the point $B(4,0).$

Given that ${\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=\frac{8}{3},$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j$ and $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the second integral, so we only need to work out the first.

The path ${C}_{1}$ is the section of the curve $y=-\sqrt{x}$ from $O$ to $A.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}(t)=t\,i-\sqrt{t}\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 4.$ Along this curve, we have $x=t$ and $y=-\sqrt{t}.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t)) & =x\,i+{y}^{2}\,j \\  & =t\,i+t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{t})j \\  & =i-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =(t\,i+t\,j)\cdot (i-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{t}}\,j) \\  & =t-\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}F({r}_{1}(t))\cdot {r}_{1}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t+\frac{8}{3} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(t-\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2})\text{d}t+\frac{8}{3} \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{t}^{3/2}}{3}]}_{0}^{4}+\frac{8}{3} \\  & =(\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{4}^{3/2}}{3}-0)+\frac{8}{3} \\  & =\frac{16}{3}+\frac{8}{3} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $F(x,y,z)={e}^{y+z}\,i+{e}^{x+z}\,j+{e}^{x+y}\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y+R(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}{e}^{y+z}\,\text{d}x+{e}^{x+z}\,\text{d}y+{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$
